project.name: thermoslim-platform
project.description: A standalone web app that unifies commerce data across Shopify, CheckoutChamp, Klaviyo, GA4, and Microsoft Clarity into a single intelligence layer — with subscription reporting, funnel analytics, automated alerts, and order QA.

nodes.name: Sidebar.tsx
nodes.summary: Client Component that renders the fixed left-side navigation sidebar for the dashboard shell. Defines a static NAV config with five grouped sections (Overview, Subscriptions, Orders, Performance, Operations) and highlights the active route via usePathname.

nodes.name: Sidebar
nodes.summary: Renders the full sidebar UI with logo header, grouped nav links with active-state highlighting, and a bottom Settings link. Uses usePathname to detect active route.

nodes.name: SyncButton.tsx

nodes.name: handleSync

nodes.name: TopBar.tsx

nodes.name: TopBar
nodes.summary: Renders the full top bar with page title derived from pathname, preset date-range buttons, custom date inputs with apply, and the SyncButton component.

nodes.name: applyPreset
nodes.summary: Translates a preset day-count code into concrete from/to date strings and calls apply() to push updated URL params. Handles special codes for Today (-2), Tomorrow (-3), YTD (-1), and All (0).

nodes.name: RollingChart

nodes.name: AnomalyCard

layers.name: UI Layer
layers.description: Dashboard pages, chart components, layouts, and loading states — the Next.js App Router frontend that renders KPI cards, data tables, and Recharts visualizations

layers.name: API Layer
layers.description: Next.js API route handlers for sync triggers, cron jobs, webhook receivers, and QA endpoints

layers.name: Data Adapter Layer
layers.description: Platform-specific data source connectors (Shopify, CheckoutChamp, Clarity, GA4, Klaviyo) that implement the adapter pattern for normalizing external data

layers.name: Core Engine Layer
layers.description: Ingestion pipeline, snapshot rebuilding, subscription linking, QA runner, sync worker, and shared type definitions — the backbone of data processing

layers.name: Shared Library Layer
layers.description: Reusable UI components (KpiCard, Badge, PageHeader), dashboard utilities (formatting, colors, MRR calculation, trial prices), Prisma client, config, and module barrel files

layers.name: Scripts & CLI Layer
layers.description: Operational CLI utilities for data sync, backfill, order analysis, CC QA research, anomaly detection, and the autoresearch AI pipeline

layers.name: Test Layer
layers.description: Vitest unit tests covering the autoresearch pipeline (detector, evaluator, injector, order-analyzer, validator)

tour.title: App Entry & Layout
tour.description: The application starts with app/layout.tsx (root HTML shell and providers) and app/page.tsx (root redirect). The dashboard lives under a route group (dashboard) with its own layout, sidebar navigation, and top bar. This is a Next.js App Router project — the file-system hierarchy IS the routing.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js route groups (parenthesized directories like (dashboard)) organize files without affecting URLs. All pages inside share the same layout.

tour.title: Shared UI Components
tour.description: Before diving into pages, understand the reusable building blocks. KpiCard renders metric tiles with sparklines, Badge provides status indicators, PageHeader standardizes page titles. These components appear on virtually every dashboard page — they are the highest fan-in UI nodes.

tour.title: Dashboard & Formatting Utilities
tour.description: The shared library layer provides formatting helpers (money, dates, percentages), chart color palettes, MRR calculation logic, and trial price lookups. Every dashboard page imports from these — they enforce consistent data display rules (money as dollars, dates in user TZ). The centralized calculateMrr() function is the single source of truth for MRR across all pages.
tour.languageLesson: Money is stored as cents (integers) in the database and formatted to dollars only in the frontend display layer — this avoids floating-point precision errors.

tour.title: Main Dashboard Page
tour.description: The primary dashboard page (dashboard/page.tsx) is the hub. It is a Server Component that runs parallel Prisma queries for revenue, orders, subscriptions, and anomalies, then renders KPI cards, a revenue chart, subscriber donut, and activity timeline. RevenueChart and SubscriberDonut are client-side Recharts wrappers.

tour.title: Prisma Database & Unified Schema
tour.description: All data flows through a single Prisma client instance. The unified schema normalizes orders from Shopify and CheckoutChamp into common entities with a source field. Revenue = Order.totalPrice where source IN (SHOPIFY, MERGED) and status = COMPLETE. Raw CHECKOUTCHAMP orders are duplicates and must be excluded — this dedup rule is critical.

tour.title: Data Source Adapters
tour.description: Each external platform has its own adapter implementing a standard interface: connect(), sync(), mapToSchema(). Shopify is the product master catalog. CheckoutChamp handles transactions, subscriptions, and funnels. Field-map files define how raw API fields map to the unified schema. Adding a new data source means creating a new adapter — nothing else changes.

tour.title: Ingestion Pipeline
tour.description: The ingestion pipeline is the largest and most critical file. It orchestrates: receive raw data → validate → normalize via adapter → write to unified store → trigger post-hooks (snapshot rebuild, subscription linking). The registry maps source names to adapter instances. Post-hooks handle side effects like rebuilding DailySnapshot aggregates.

tour.title: Sync & Snapshot Engine
tour.description: The sync worker processes BullMQ jobs for scheduled data pulls. rebuild-snapshots.ts rebuilds DailySnapshot pre-aggregated time-series data from deduplicated COMPLETE orders — this is the source of truth for analytics charts. link-subscriptions.ts auto-links CC subscriptions to Shopify products via the product mapping.

tour.title: API Routes & Webhooks
tour.description: API routes trigger syncs (manual and cron), receive webhooks, and expose QA endpoints. The CC cron route runs every few hours via Vercel cron, syncing recent data and firing snapshot rebuilds. Webhooks from Shopify and CC push real-time order updates through the ingestion pipeline.

tour.title: Subscription Analytics
tour.description: The subscription module provides MRR waterfall analysis, frequency distribution, cohort retention curves, and churn tracking. The MRR page uses the centralized calculateMrr() function. Cohorts group subscribers by signup month and track retention over time. Each page follows the same pattern: async server component → parallel Prisma queries → serialize → render.

tour.title: QA & Health Checks
tour.description: The QA system validates data integrity across sources. The runner executes validation rules and produces findings. Health checks monitor adapter connectivity, data freshness, and pipeline throughput. These power the operations/health and operations/qa dashboard pages.

tour.title: CC QA Research Pipeline
tour.description: The scripts/cc-qa/ directory is a sophisticated data quality toolkit. The researcher (926 lines) deep-dives into CC API data to identify discrepancies. The simulator replays CC sync logic against live data. The engine orchestrates multi-step QA workflows. These are CLI tools for operational investigation, not part of the web app.

tour.title: Autoresearch AI Pipeline
tour.description: The autoresearch pipeline uses Claude AI to analyze order anomalies. The detector identifies suspicious patterns, the order-analyzer deep-dives individual orders, and the cascade-runner chains multiple analysis passes. Results feed back into the platform as acknowledged or escalated anomalies.
